title: Awards season: Gotham, NYFCC and NBR predictions
body_md:
The first major week of the 2026 film awards season is approaching, with the Gotham Awards, New York Film Critics Circle and National Board of Review poised to offer early signals about a crowded Oscar race. A published set of forecasts suggests that independent dramas, ambitious studio productions and documentary filmmaking could receive very different kinds of support from these organizations.

**The selections below are editorial predictions, not announced winners or official voting results.**

## Gotham Awards: The Invite leads the forecast

Olivia Wilde's The Invite is the projected best feature winner at the Gothams, with Josephine identified as the alternative. The latter's earlier success at Sundance makes it a plausible contender in an organization that has frequently recognized discoveries from the independent film circuit.

Ryusuke Hamaguchi is the predicted directing winner for All of a Sudden. Andrew Scott is favored for lead performance in Elsinore, while Tao Okamoto leads the supporting performance forecast for All of a Sudden. The Gothams use separate juries for different categories, so their results need not follow a single consensus across the entire ballot.

## New York critics: A documentary challenges The Odyssey

The forecast for the New York Film Critics Circle places You Can See Everything ahead of Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey for best film. Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's documentary about Elizabeth Holmes could receive a significant boost if it wins an award usually associated with narrative features.

Wilde is the predicted directing winner, with Nolan listed as the alternative. Scott is again favored for acting recognition, while Julianne Moore leads the actress forecast for The Debut. Robert Pattinson and Sandra Huller are among the potential alternatives in the acting races.

## National Board of Review: Project Hail Mary

Project Hail Mary is the projected best film winner at the National Board of Review, ahead of Artificial. Its directors, Phil Lord and Christopher Miller, also lead the directing forecast, with Denis Villeneuve considered a possible alternative for Dune: Part Three.

Seth Rogen is the predicted actor winner for The Invite, and Inde Navarrette leads the actress forecast for Obsession. Wildwood is favored in animation.

These early prizes matter because they replace months of festival reactions and speculative campaigning with actual voting outcomes. Nevertheless, the organizations have different memberships, eligibility rules and artistic priorities. Their selections should be interpreted as individual endorsements rather than a definitive ranking of Oscar contenders.

The strongest signal may be a film's ability to build support across several independent voting groups. Until the awards are announced, however, these remain informed guesses rather than established facts.

[Source forecasts](https://variety.com/lists/gotham-nyfcc-nbr-afi-lafca-predictions-2026)
